answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every identity to post a bonded stake that peers can slash. To vote or earn rewards, an agent locks collateral; honest service returns it, but a detected clone or double vote destroys it. Validators vouch with their own bonds, so endorsing an army of fakes puts their capital at risk too. Like a quill etched into a walnut shell, each identity leaves a mark too costly to forge cheaply. The harbor stays safe because minting a thousand impostors means posting a thousand bonds, while each honest captain risks the very collateral it guards.
